title: Finite assembly frontier, exact bank optimization, and E8 verification
body:
Fixed backoffs and a fixed bootstrap depth leave an avoidable gap below the balanced assembly's supplied-cap ceiling. This PR adds a constructive theorem and exact verifier that select finite parameters for **every rational target below `min(b,c)/(1+min(b,c))`**, given admitted bit and complex caps and the retained conditional interfaces.

The [new package](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/2a9aac19031199025c3a3f7e1a6c3c14b81ce6a3/research/finite-assembly-frontier) chooses strictly positive backoffs, a finite number of bootstrap steps and explicit integer cutoffs. The [proof](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2a9aac19031199025c3a3f7e1a6c3c14b81ce6a3/research/finite-assembly-frontier/PROOF.md) establishes termination and all 47 retained strict outer inequalities. It also proves maximality on a supplied rational grid, relative to these caps and this assembly family. The ceiling itself is not attained.

### Current worked example

Using the unchanged suppliers from [PR433](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/433), pinned to `6d9244518175caf9e0089f92486959bc2c317273`, the greatest admitted point on a `10^-27` grid is

```
kappa = 280216238064569651155257 / 250000000000000000000000000
      = 0.001120864952258278604621028
```

This is strictly above that source's `0.001120864952258278`, by approximately **6.04621e-19**. The numerical gain is tiny. The reusable parameter theorem and verifier are the main contribution; no new supplier word, practical speedup or global optimality is claimed. Later supplier contributions, including [PR434](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/434), report higher bounds. This pinned example is not a claim to the current numerical lead; the parameter theorem applies to future admitted caps as well.

One clean default replay of the pinned supplier package passed all 13 stages in 6.19 seconds. It regenerated both changed programs, their scalar and ownership checks, moments and finite invoices; the original verifier reused its source-bound Gaussian phase evidence. We did not rerun every Gaussian pair. Actual receipts and all stage logs are retained. The new verifier independently reproduces the original assembly, recomputes both supplier moments and the selected seed with two rational engines, checks the actual 483-bit two-level coefficient against its 512-bit charge, and verifies nine finite bootstrap steps and all 47 strict inequalities. The next grid point, zero eta, zero beta and unit beta are rejected.

Five focused tests cover both binding components, equal caps, 48 cap/target regimes, exact grid endpoints, 100-digit grids, zero-step cases and invalid premises. Ody independently reviewed the proof and code and reran the complete package successfully. All 50 package inputs match manifest `876412045fcd74e87bba4f02704eb312fad77e565e73eecb1c4849e1df92ff8d`. The CLI also exports witnesses whose rational numerators exceed Python’s default decimal conversion limit; an end-to-end 100-digit-grid regression covers this. An integration test connects this offline verifier to the existing Python 3.11/3.13/3.14 test matrix, without a new workflow or executor.

```sh
python3 -B research/finite-assembly-frontier/verify.py
```

Add `--output /absolute/path/to/new-result.json` to retain every exact parameter, cutoff and margin. Python 3.11+ and the standard library suffice.

**Current signed head:** `2a9aac19031199025c3a3f7e1a6c3c14b81ce6a3`. Local package verification and the repository integration test pass. **CI for this new head is pending.** The previous head `3d575f5b373cf3f49219b95d2dd00db4cf314e8d` passed all 56 repository jobs: [research/formal](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38135823526), [terminal elimination](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38135823529), [recycled registers](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38135823525). Those results are historical, not new-head validation.

### Earlier contributions retained

- [Exact bank optimizer](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/2a9aac19031199025c3a3f7e1a6c3c14b81ce6a3/research/e8-exact-bank-optimizer): necessary-and-sufficient packing conditions, optimal patterns and minimum replication for the width-73 rank family. An independent exhaustive oracle checks 16,875 inventories.
- [Chart-sensitive dirty-endpoint audit](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/2a9aac19031199025c3a3f7e1a6c3c14b81ce6a3/research/e8-dirty-chart-audit): exact all-address Gaussian checking, including a counterexample invisible at address zero and an admitted positive control. Six focused regressions pass. Its obstruction is scoped to the stated independent-bank interface.
- [E8 retimed component verification](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/2a9aac19031199025c3a3f7e1a6c3c14b81ce6a3/research/e8-retimed-component-verification): retained emitter, phase, lifetime and finite-accounting evidence for the pinned PR384 complex component.
- [Weighted donor-rank matching](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/2a9aac19031199025c3a3f7e1a6c3c14b81ce6a3/research/gen5b-weighted-matching): the earlier reproducible construction reused by later contributions. Its historical conditional bound is `0.000751075693834608`; later suppliers improve it.

The supplier compiler, compressed-window, arbitrary dirty-bank, restored-work, fixed-tape/common-grid, precision and analytic interfaces remain assumptions. This is a conditional finite construction, with no unconditional multiplication theorem or new Lean proof.

New parameter selection, proof, tests and evidence integration: George Lydakis with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including Ody's independent review. PR433's construction remains credited to icekylinx with OpenAI Codex; its upstream lineage includes Zhihao Chen, ai-nanachi, Dylan Crow, Jacob Sussman and the retained contributors. The unchanged outer engine retains its eumemic/Anthropic Claude, icekylinx, Zhihao Chen and RaD/hipotures credits. Original notices, licenses, source pins and earlier package attribution are preserved.
